### 🔴 E-1: F# compile order is wrong — `BrokenOrder.fsproj` will fail to compile
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- ← uses Domain types -->
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- ← defines Domain types -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

In F#, file order is significant — files can only reference types defined in files listed **above** them. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` (defined in `Domain.fs`), but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This will produce a compile error (`FS0039: The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`).

**Fix:** Reorder to `Domain.fs` → `Services.fs` → `Program.fs` (as `OrderService.fsproj` correctly does).

---

### 🔴 E-2: `TreatWarningsAsErrors` in `Directory.Build.targets` silently overrides project-level opt-outs
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, line 7  
**Victim:** `LibB/LibB.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets (imported AFTER .csproj) -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>

<!-- LibB.csproj (set in project, but gets overwritten) -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

MSBuild evaluation order is: `Directory.Build.props` → SDK `.props` → `.csproj` → SDK `.targets` → `Directory.Build.targets`. Since `.targets` is evaluated last, the unconditional assignment in `Directory.Build.targets` **always wins**, making LibB's opt-out a dead setting.

**Fix:** Move this property (and `Company`, `Authors`, `Copyright`) to `Directory.Build.props` with a conditional default:
```xml
<TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

### 🔴 E-3: `DefineConstants` is overwritten instead of appended
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 13–14

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

This **replaces** the SDK-provided constants (`TRACE`, `DEBUG`) with only `ENABLE_LOGGING`. Any code gated on `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

### 🔴 E-4: Unquoted `Condition` attribute — evaluation hazard
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

The value is not quoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during restore or evaluation outside a solution context), the condition evaluates to ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression and causes an **MSB4100 evaluation error**. Even when non-empty, this is a well-known gotcha.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

### 🔴 E-5: `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` — always false for single-TFM projects (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 10–12

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

For single-targeting projects (all projects here), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation — it's only populated during the inner build. This condition never matches, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is **never set**. This is a silent, hard-to-diagnose bug.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets` where `$(TargetFramework)` is populated:
```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 🔴 E-6: Publish-on-build target forks a second project instance — race condition
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

This re-invokes the same project with an added global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), creating a **second MSBuild project instance** that resolves to the same `OutputPath` and `IntermediateOutputPath`. The two instances race to write the same files, causing intermittent I/O failures (especially under `-m` parallel builds).

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish in the *same* project instance, with a cycle guard:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishOnBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" Condition="'$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'">
  <!-- publish logic here, or set _IsPublishing and invoke Publish via DependsOnTargets -->
</Target>
```

### 🟡 W-1: Hardcoded Windows-absolute `OutputPath`
**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7, `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

This is a Windows-only absolute path. It will:
- Fail on Linux/macOS CI (the path is meaningless on Unix)
- Fail for any developer whose `C:` drive layout differs
- Bypass the SDK's standard `bin/$(Configuration)/$(TargetFramework)` convention, breaking `dotnet pack` and other tooling expectations

**Fix:** Use relative paths or SDK defaults:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\artifacts\LibA\</OutputPath>
```
Or better, remove entirely and let the SDK manage output paths.

### 🟡 W-2: Legacy `<Reference>` with `<HintPath>` to a `packages\` folder
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

This is a `packages.config`-style assembly reference pointing at a vendored `packages\` folder. In an SDK-style project this is incorrect — NuGet PackageReference is the proper mechanism. The `net6.0` binary in the hint path is also mismatched with the project's `net8.0` TFM.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 🟡 W-3: Analyzer package leaks to downstream consumers
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 16–18

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, any project that references LibA or LibB as a NuGet package will transitively pull in StyleCop.Analyzers, running StyleCop rules in the *consumer's* build — almost certainly unintended.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 🟡 W-4: Redundant `<Compile Include>` creates duplicate item — CS2002
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 21–24

```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

The SDK auto-globs all `*.cs` files, so `Class1.cs` is already in the `Compile` item list. The explicit `Include` adds a **second** entry, which triggers **CS2002** ("Source file 'Class1.cs' specified multiple times"). The `Update` then only modifies one of the two entries.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 🟡 W-5: Custom target `PrintVersion` has no `Inputs`/`Outputs` — breaks incremental builds
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

Without `Inputs`/`Outputs`, this target runs on **every** build, even when nothing changed. This defeats incremental build optimization and will appear as wasted time in build performance analysis. Additionally, the version is hardcoded — it won't track actual project version changes.

**Fix:** Either add `Inputs`/`Outputs` to make it incremental, or if it's truly informational, accept the cost but document the intent.

---

### 🟡 W-6: Property defaults in `Directory.Build.targets` instead of `.props`
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 8–10

```xml
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Build Team</Authors>
<Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
```

Even beyond `TreatWarningsAsErrors` (E-2), these metadata properties are **defaults** — they belong in `Directory.Build.props` where projects can override them. In `.targets`, they silently win over any project-level customization.

**Fix:** Move all four properties to `Directory.Build.props` with conditional defaults.

### 🟡 W-7: Solution file doesn't include F# projects
**File:** `StyleIssues.sln`

The solution only references `LibA` and `LibB`. The `fsharp/BrokenOrder` and `fsharp/OrderService` projects are not included. This means:
- `dotnet build StyleIssues.sln` won't build the F# projects
- CI pipelines using the solution file will miss them entirely
- The F# projects won't receive solution-level `Configuration`/`Platform` global properties

### 🟡 W-8: No Central Package Management
**Files:** `Directory.Build.props` line 17, `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 28

Package versions are scattered across individual files. With multiple projects, this leads to version drift and diamond-dependency conflicts.

**Fix:** Create `Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` and move all versions there.
